sections.title: 1. Executive Verdict
sections.text: Completed conditional review: BQS 4.42, growth-quality GQS 4.30, IAS 3.25. IPO-funded output growth has not yet produced strong cash realization; diluted EPS fell despite group profit growth. Central modeled IRR is 8.6%, below the 15% research hurdle. Funding dependence and poor observed trading capacity dominate the investment assessment. [S1–S3, M1]

sections.title: 2. Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: As of 20 October 2026. B. D. Industries (Pune) Limited is BSE SME code 544468, ISIN INE1LJ801017, originally listed August 7, 2025. September AGM corroborates 14,210,000 shares; the October 19 NSE master identifies a BSE-listed BDI$ instrument with 1,200 lot. Its April 2026 master date is not original BSE admission. ₹123 on October 16 is a secondary dated close, not live or official BSE pricing. [S1, S2, S7, M1, M_SECURITY_SPEC]

sections.title: 3. Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: GOV 4, MOAT 5, REV 4, DUR 6, CAP 3, CASH 3, BAL 6, EXEC 5 and EARN 5. IAS uses final BQS plus R 3, D 3, P 4 and L 1. REV uses same-parent history, not mixed acquisition scope. Recent low CAP/CASH are not automatically called persistent full-cycle destruction. Exact weights and contrary evidence are retained in the audit.

sections.title: 4. Business Overview
sections.text: Rotationally moulded plastic products serve automotive OEMs, material handling, safety and renewable applications. Listed parent owns Pune; Dewas and Hoshiarpur came through B.D. Industries (India), acquired September 30, 2024 from promoter directors for ₹6.6529 crore. FY26 manufacturing sales ₹83.7865 crore and traded goods ₹16.8351 crore show a predominantly manufacturing group, not a pure patented-product franchise. [S1, S2]

sections.title: 5. Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: OEM qualifications, custom moulds and plants near customers can create relationship stickiness. Against this, FY25 group top customer was 33.04% of sales, top five 63.48% and top ten 75.83%; top ten suppliers were 80.45%. Earlier parent concentration is a different scope. Renewable-product patent claims were not independently validated; a trademark is not proof of enforceable technology exclusivity. [S2, S6]

sections.title: 6. Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Group revenue rose ₹82.3785 crore to ₹100.6448 crore, while the same parent rose ₹54.0902 crore to ₹64.4373 crore. Parent FY24 sales ₹54.2502 crore imply about 9% two-year CAGR. Group PAT rose ₹7.6753 crore to ₹9.5558 crore, but weighted EPS fell ₹7.67 to ₹7.48 and full post-issue historical EPS is about ₹6.72. IPO-restated figures are not spliced into annual cash ratios. [S1, S2]

sections.title: 7. Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: CWIP-inclusive incremental return is about 5.4%, or 6.0% excluding CWIP, below an assumed 12–16% capital hurdle. IPO funds precede mature output, so this is not a lifetime project IRR. FY26 reported output Pune 1,399 MT, Dewas 963 MT and Hoshiarpur 613 MT implies 77.7%, 64.2% and 51.1% utilization. The presentation specifies proposed Zaheerabad capacity 750 MT and a 2026 launch, not verified commercial completion. The April ₹10.08 crore spacer order includes tax and was due August 31; performance and receipts remain unverified. [S1, S2, S4, S6]

sections.title: 8. Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: FY26 CMD ₹1.20 crore, whole-time director ₹0.2957 crore and commissions of ₹0.30 crore each to Akshay and Rahul total ₹2.0957 crore before other fees, about 21.9% of group PAT. Related Aara rent was ₹0.60 crore and related interest-free loan repayments ₹5.4561 crore. September 29 AGM approved Akshay’s commission ceiling increasing to ₹0.60 crore annually for April 2026–March 2029; the tally includes promoter votes, with 2,400 public votes against. This is an approved ceiling, not proof it was all paid or a legal finding about voting. August issuer disclosure reports Acuité B−/A4 issuer-not-cooperating while asserting the rated Union Bank facilities were repaid and an NOC obtained; independent agency withdrawal/NOC was not verified. [S1–S3, S7]

sections.title: 9. Financial Forensics
sections.text: FY26 CFO of −₹11.3871 crore is reconciled to balance changes and signed entity statements. The apparent trade-balance mismatch reflects approximately ₹5.1046 crore matching intercompany elimination movements plus noncash write-backs/write-offs; tax/advance/provision lines also reconcile in combination. The complete reconstruction equals reported CFO. Two-year reported CFO/PAT is about −0.075, or −0.073 when FY25 pre-acquisition profit is restored for a full-year cash-scope sensitivity. Inventory ₹41.9014 crore and receivables ₹28.0003 crore remain cash-intensive; ₹3.9750 crore of receivables exceed six months. Separately, standalone bank-reported March receivables exceed books by ₹5.8605 crore. The issuer cites timing/regrouping and unchanged drawing power; this is not independently confirmed or called fraud. Opening net tax ₹4.3185 crore is explicitly paid in the model. [S1, S8, S9] Opening-claim audit: operating statutory, payroll and expense liabilities of ₹1.9342 crore and current employee/expense provisions of ₹0.0891 crore are already included in opening and forecast operating WC. They are not charged again as separate debt. Opening tax/interest settlement remains ₹4.3185 crore net of tax advances. Noncurrent employee liabilities of ₹0.4866 crore are outside operating WC and are now deducted once from terminal equity, held at the opening net obligation with no assumed plan-asset recovery. Future service cost remains within forecast operating expenses. Existing bank principal remains in the debt schedule and terminal debt; no duplicate current-maturity deduction is made. [S1]

sections.title: 10. Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: Secondary October 16 price ₹123 and 14.21 million shares imply ₹174.783 crore market capitalization and 18.29 times FY26 PAT. Actual-opening funded bear/base/bull IRRs are -18.0%/8.6%/30.4%. Base assumes 12% sales growth, 13% EBIT margin and 13-times EV/EBIT exit, with current WC intensity retained. The hurdle needs about 16.8 times exit EV/EBIT at central operations. All forecasts include taxes, capex, debt service, conditional funding, dilution and terminal equity claims. [S1–S3, S6, S7, M1] The terminal bridge additionally retains the audited legacy employee and deferred-tax claims; the annual operating and financing schedules are unchanged. [S1]

sections.title: 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: Customer loss, resin-price pressure, slow collections and underutilized assets can force repeated funding. A 10% inventory/receivable cash replacement stress is ₹6.9902 crore, not a reported impairment. Ordinary bear terminal equity loss is 62.8%; no-new-credit and overdraft-call cases explicitly model rescue needs. IPO funds are historical, not a repeatable war chest. Only ₹2.3405 crore unused IPO proceeds remained at March 31, overlapping cash/deposits. [S1–S3]

sections.title: 12. 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Five-year 5× and 10× outcomes require 37.97% and 58.49% annual per-share returns. Recent diluted EPS declined despite profit growth. Even the bull depends on 20% sustained sales growth, 16% EBIT margin, improved WC and a 17-times exit. Five times is demanding and ten times unsupported by the modeled path; no success probability is assigned.

sections.title: 13. Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Monitor Zaheerabad commissioning and utilization, spacer delivery and receipts, inventory age, collection performance, bank/book reconciliations, updated rating/NOC evidence and related pay. Observed-row median low price times volume is ₹4.566 lakh: ₹5 lakh needs approximately 21.90 days at 5%, 54.75 at 2% and 10.95 at 10%. This is neither actual traded value nor a complete 60-session measure. No live spread, depth or comprehensive BSE surveillance clearance is asserted. [S1, S3, S4, S6, M1]

sections.title: 14. Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Conditional industrial-expansion watchlist, not a buy recommendation. Low current incremental returns, negative cash conversion, expensive funding dependence and poor observed liquidity limit attractiveness. A dated secondary quote is usable only with these limitations; it is not an executable offer.

sections.title: 15. Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Annual/prospectus, May presentation, April order, June resignation, August rating disclosure and September AGM voting were reviewed. Signed May results and subsidiary statements resolve the consolidated gross cash-flow reconciliation; its separate bank-report explanation remains issuer-reported. Issuer index was refreshed on October 20. A secondary September open-market stake-acquisition lead was not independently retrieved; it is not treated as dilution, and AGM/master capital is separately corroborated. Remaining uncertainties concern actual project completion, collections, credit renewal and BSE execution depth. [S1–S9, M1, M_SECURITY_SPEC]

valuation.IAS_status: Conditional on the dated secondary quote, verified capital/lot corroboration and ₹5 lakh reference; weak observed liquidity and uncommitted financing are explicitly scored, not silently ignored.
assumptions: Units are INR crore and crore shares. March 2026 consolidated actuals open the model; the IPO already appears in historical accounts and is NOT credited again. Five full operating years approximate October 2026 to October 2031. No dividends are assumed.

Opening operating WC is inventory 41.9014 + receivables 28.0003 + short advances 9.6703 + other current assets 0.5821 − payables 18.3380 − other current liabilities 1.9342 − tax advances 1.0378 − interest receivable 0.0080 − employee provisions 0.0891 = 58.7470. Tax advances are netted against opening income-tax provision 5.3563, giving year-one payment 4.3185. Future modeled tax is on future earnings only.

Opening cash equivalents 3.9679 exclude bank deposits 2.4507 throughout. IPO escrow 1.5254 within cash is restricted to eligible project spending; first-year project spend exceeds that amount. No separate credit is taken for unused IPO funds. Year-one tax and spending create an explicit need for finance; intrayear timing may require a bridge before cash collection.

Additional project allowance 6.6129 is an analyst completion/equipment allowance, not a disclosed remaining commitment and not a second expenditure of historical CWIP. Zero and double allowances bound this uncertainty. Base 12% revenue growth can be interpreted as approximately 9% volume and 3% realization/mix; 2,975 MT initial output would reach about 4,577 MT, below existing plus proposed 750 MT Zaheerabad capacity of 5,250 MT. Completion and demand are assumptions, not verified orders.

Base EBIT margin 13% is below FY26 operating EBIT margin approximately 14.55%, allowing for increased commission and execution costs. It is not the headline margin including written-back balances. The 13-times terminal EV/EBIT multiple is an explicit assumption near entry enterprise value divided by historical operating EBIT, not a current peer median.

Existing overdrafts 16.4315 are revolving demand credit, not amortizing term loans. First-year term principal 0.5223 comes from current maturities; remaining term principal 0.5659 is spread over four years as a bounded approximation. Renewal and recall are separately stressed. Neither an old Union Bank discharge claim nor a security-master row proves credit availability.

Growth capex is the greater of 70%/30% project allowance and incremental sales divided by assumed incremental fixed-asset turnover. Maintenance equals depreciation; growth-asset depreciation uses ten years and a half-year convention. Annual WC is a stock, and only its change uses cash.

Forecast cash tax is 25.17% of positive PBT. Half-year interest on repayment and new debt is solved with financing needs. Cash floor is 5% of sales. Assumed debt capacity is 30% of sales; additional deficits issue equity at half the observed price. These are conditional financing rules, not committed facilities. A no-new-credit case tests the rating-information risk.

Terminal EV is year-five EBIT times the assumed multiple, less all bank debt, plus cash above the operating floor, divided by fully diluted shares. Terminal IRR is (terminal price / 123)^(1/5) minus one. Severe stress also pays contingent guarantee 0.1725 and tax demand 0.5045; neither is called a realized loss.

Secondary OHLCV covers 34 observed rows, not a verified complete 60-session series. Low price times volume is an approximate lower turnover bound, not reported traded value. Missing rows are not assumed zero. The L score reflects poor observed capacity and incomplete coverage, rather than representing a precise full-window estimate.

Opening-claim audit: operating statutory, payroll and expense liabilities of ₹1.9342 crore and current employee/expense provisions of ₹0.0891 crore are already included in opening and forecast operating WC. They are not charged again as separate debt. Opening tax/interest settlement remains ₹4.3185 crore net of tax advances. Noncurrent employee liabilities of ₹0.4866 crore are outside operating WC and are now deducted once from terminal equity, held at the opening net obligation with no assumed plan-asset recovery. Future service cost remains within forecast operating expenses. Existing bank principal remains in the debt schedule and terminal debt; no duplicate current-maturity deduction is made.

GOV.reason: Related pay, rent and promoter acquisition are quantified. September AGM approved doubling Akshay Saini’s commission ceiling to ₹0.60 crore; promoter votes are included in the reported tally. Rating noncooperation and bank/book reconciliation constrain confidence. These are capital-allocation and control risks, not findings of diversion or unlawful voting.

MOAT.reason: OEM customization and geographic plants create qualification relationships; top customer 33% and high supplier concentration limit bargaining power.

REV.reason: The scored longer-history proxy is same-parent FY24–FY26 CAGR of about 9%, mapping to 4. Group FY26 growth of 22.17% is positive contrary evidence. The group comparative presents full-year combined operating figures with a separate pre-acquisition profit deduction; no mixed FY24-parent/FY26-group CAGR is used. A group-only one-year proxy would score higher, so this scope choice is explicit.

DUR.reason: Spare capacity, rising output and specific new spacer order support runway; commissioning/collections and customer concentration remain contrary evidence.

CAP.reason: CWIP-inclusive incremental return of about 5.4% is below the assumed 12–16% capital hurdle. Excluding CWIP leaves the result weak, but immature IPO-funded investment is not a full-cycle project failure finding.

CASH.reason: CFO is genuinely negative after the documented intercompany/noncash/tax reconciliation, not a naïve gross-line mismatch. Two-year reported conversion is about −0.075; using FY25 profit before its pre-acquisition deduction gives −0.073, still weak. FY25 positive CFO prevents an automatic persistent-destruction override.

BAL.reason: IPO expanded equity ₹71.71 crore and book debt declined ₹17.52 crore; restricted deposits, working-capital use and rating-information uncertainty constrain comfort.

EXEC.reason: Plant outputs increased and acquisition integrated; diluted EPS fell and cash conversion weakened while new site remains unconfirmed.

EARN.reason: Group PAT grew 24.5%, but share dilution, pre-acquisition scope and written-back balances weaken simple growth extrapolation.

R.reason: Central conditional five-year IRR 8.57% after all identified opening claims is -6.43 percentage points below/above the 15% hurdle, mapping to R=3. Forecasts and terminal tax timing remain assumptions.

D.reason: Ordinary bear loses 62.8% of equity value, with substantial new debt. A no-new-credit case needs additional equity, and forced overdraft withdrawal is worse. Recapitalization is conditional, not assured.

P.reason: Central operations need about 16.8 times terminal EV/EBIT to reach a 15% hurdle versus 13 times modeled. Execution and margin improvement or rerating must bridge the gap; modest misses damage returns.

L.reason: Among 34 observed sessions, median low-price-times-volume is ₹4.566 lakh. ₹5 lakh at 5% participation implies 21.90 observed-session days; 2% and 10% imply 54.75 and 10.95. This already starts in the lowest band; incomplete coverage, ₹147,600 lot, absent depth and unverified BSE surveillance prevent an upgrade. It is not a complete 60-session estimate.

gates.reason: Promoter acquisition, related remuneration/rent and approved commission increase merit a below-average governance score. Reviewed disclosures do not substantiate severe diversion. Rating and bank-reconciliation concerns remain explicit.

Signed results and subsidiary statements corroborate annual totals. The apparent cash-flow/balance differences reconcile when matching intercompany eliminations, write-backs/write-offs and tax/advance grouping are combined. A complete reconstruction equals reported CFO. Separate bank-report differences retain the issuer’s explanation and remain a monitoring caveat, not a proven cash-flow overstatement.

The base requires additional borrowing despite historical IPO funding; ordinary and severe cases expose refinancing dependence. No-new-credit and full-overdraft-call tests permit only conditional equity rescue. Unverified Union Bank discharge is not treated as a funding guarantee.

AGM capital of 14,210,000 shares and current master lot 1,200 corroborate a reference valuation. Three lots cost ₹442,800 versus ₹5 lakh reference. Dated secondary trades do not establish complete BSE surveillance or live execution. Low capacity is scored L=1; no position-size recommendation is made.
